title: DESIGN AND PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION OF A PLASMA–OZONE REACTOR WITH PLATINUM ELECTRODES FOR THE INDUSTRIAL TREATMENT OF GROUNDWATER IN SEISMICALLY ACTIVE MOUNTAINOUS REGIONS

DESIGN AND PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION OF A PLASMA–OZONE REACTOR WITH PLATINUM ELECTRODES FOR THE INDUSTRIAL TREATMENT OF GROUNDWATER IN SEISMICALLY ACTIVE MOUNTAINOUS REGIONS

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Yerik Alipuly, Indira Abilakhanova, Akerke Yerkinova, Almukhan Nuraliyev
Print ISSN : 2523-5664

ABSTRACT

This article presents a design configuration and performance optimization method for a plasma–ozone reactor equipped with platinum electrodes for the industrial treatment of groundwater in seismically active mountainous regions. The reactor integrates a high-voltage plasma discharge unit, ozone injection, Venturi mixing, a contact chamber, residual ozone neutralization, post-filtration, and automated monitoring units. The raw water was characterized by pH = 6,35, ORP = +78 mV, EC = 1290 μS/cm, TDS = 825 mg/L, Fe²⁺ = 5,30 mg/L, Mn²⁺ = 1,72 mg/L, NH₄⁺ – N = 6,50 mg/L, COD = 50 mg/L, and E. coli = 1,0 · 10⁴ CFU/mL. The optimal operating regime was determined within the ranges U = 14,5 – 15,0 kV, f = 9,8-10,5 kHz, O₃ = 60-65 mg/L, Qw = 5,2-5,6 m³/h, and τ = 24-28 min. Under these conditions, Fe²⁺ removal reached 97.7%, Mn²⁺ removal 94.8%, NH₄⁺ – N reduction 87,7%, COD removal 84.0%, and microbiological inactivation 99,9%. Specific power consumption amounted to 0,36-0,42 kWh/m³ and the ozone utilization factor was 78-84 %. The obtained results indicated that the integrated effect of plasma and ozone makes it possible to achieve stable treatment of groundwater with a complicated iron-manganese-ammonium nitrogen – COD matrix composition.
